chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: A newspaper claim about quitting to marry, 1942
summary: An Institute clipping said she'd retire; she married a doctor in 1942 during Le Ruban Bleu.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Okay. Let me just back-track for one moment here, before we go into the time you appeared at the Le Ruban Bleu. In one of the Institute of Jazz Studies files there's an unidentified press clipping and I don't think it's dated. It says, 'sometime around June the 15th, 1941 Maxine Sullivan announces that she's going to retire'. I wonder if you have any recollection of that.

That must have been at the same time the reporter asked me if I was going to include "Loch Lomond" in my repertoire and I said, 'not if I can help it'. Then I had just come off the road too and that was a real crazy experience for me and I thought it was time to retire. I was tired. And I guess I was tired of doing "Loch Lomond".
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And this was to a doctor?

Yes. In fact that might have been, no if it stated 1941 I didn't make that remark. When I got married I might have said that because I decided I was going to stay home during that time, and I did stay home for quite a spell, maybe a year; but then I went back to work again. I didn't, well so far the arrangement we did . . .
This was after the Le Ruban Bleu?

No, this was during the Ruban Bleu. This was '42, during the time I was at the Le Ruban Bleu. It was right after I came off the tour with Benny Carter, see? Because when I came back, I mean I had been divorced from Kirby.
So maybe this clipping was dated late '41 and they were talking about next June of '42.
It might have. I'm not sure. I don't know anything about the article. I don't even

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

remember having made that remark, but I might have be- (Laughs) cause I was always retiring. I thought, you know, really someone had mentioned to me when I - when things started happening for me, "Loch Lomond" and Hollywood and movies, somebody said, you know, you're only going to be around, be on top for two years and after that it's all down hill. So I figured I had already overstayed my time. But somebody was wrong somewhere. But if you'll notice, so far as the show business is concerned you do, you know, you hit the peak and then you stay on top until you use your luck. It doesn't mean you're not popular. It just means you can't be number one.
Well, that was obviously, it was a bad time in entertainment.
